subject: Biology
description: Malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Japanese encephalitis, filaria, kala-azar — pathogen + vector + control

questions.stem: Malaria is caused by which group of organisms?
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites — single-celled protozoans. Five species infect humans: P. falciparum (most lethal), P. vivax (most common in India), P. malariae, P. ovale, P. knowlesi. Vector — female Anopheles mosquito. Nobel 1902 — Ronald Ross (Secunderabad, India) identified the mosquito-malaria link. World Malaria Day: 25 April.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Dengue fever is transmitted by which mosquito?
questions.explanation: Dengue — RNA virus (Flavivirus family), 4 serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4) — spread by female Aedes aegypti (day-biting, urban breeder in stagnant water). Aedes also carries chikungunya, Zika, yellow fever. Anopheles — malaria. Culex — Japanese encephalitis, filariasis, West Nile. Only FEMALE mosquitoes bite (need blood for egg development); males feed on nectar.

questions.stem: The vector for Japanese Encephalitis (JE) in India is:
questions.explanation: Japanese Encephalitis — Flavivirus (same genus as dengue). Primary vector in India is Culex tritaeniorhynchus (rice-paddy breeder). Pigs and waterbirds act as amplifying hosts; humans are dead-end hosts. Endemic in paddy-growing regions of UP, Bihar, Assam, West Bengal, Odisha. JE vaccine part of Universal Immunization Programme since 2006 in endemic districts.

questions.stem: Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is transmitted by the bite of:
questions.explanation: Kala-azar — 'black fever' in Hindi — is caused by Leishmania donovani protozoan. Vector — female Phlebotomus argentipes sandfly (smaller than a mosquito, active at dusk/dawn). Endemic in Bihar, Jharkhand, WB, UP — India, Bangladesh and Nepal signed a tripartite elimination MoU in 2005. Treatment: liposomal amphotericin B (single dose programme in endemic areas).

questions.stem: Which disease is caused by the parasitic worm Wuchereria bancrofti, transmitted by Culex mosquitoes?
questions.explanation: Lymphatic filariasis — chronic parasitic infection by microscopic worms (Wuchereria bancrofti causes 90% of cases, Brugia malayi the rest). Adult worms block lymph vessels → severe swelling of legs, arms, scrotum (hydrocele) — the disfigurement called elephantiasis. Mass Drug Administration (MDA) programme uses DEC + albendazole + ivermectin to eliminate transmission. India's target — eliminate by 2027.

questions.stem: Which Plasmodium species is responsible for the most severe and fatal form of malaria?
questions.explanation: P. falciparum — the deadliest Plasmodium species — causes cerebral malaria by sequestering infected RBCs in brain capillaries. Fatality if untreated. Most common globally in sub-Saharan Africa; in India, ~50% of malaria cases are falciparum (NE states, Odisha, Chhattisgarh). P. vivax is more common in India overall but rarely fatal. Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) is first-line for falciparum.

questions.stem: Chikungunya virus belongs to which family, and what is its most characteristic symptom?
questions.explanation: Chikungunya — an RNA virus in Togaviridae family, genus Alphavirus. Name is Makonde (Tanzania) for 'that which bends up' — reflects the stooped posture caused by severe, prolonged arthralgia (joint pain) which can persist for months. Dengue is Flaviviridae. Rabies is Rhabdoviridae. COVID is Coronaviridae. Vector — same as dengue: Aedes aegypti + Aedes albopictus.
